**Dallas County Data Questions and Responses:**

- There appears to be a small number of referrals with multiple supervision records (in the supervision file) -- how should we interpret this?

- Do new violations (whether new offenses or technical violations) that occur while a youth is on supervision always result in a new referral ID? It looks like this is the case in briefing looking through the violations data -- is joining by individual ID and then using dates to determine if a given violation occurred during a period of supervision the best way to merge these two files? The data dictionary you all provided indicates that the referral number in the violations data file can be used for "Identifying number of the referral to which the listed VOP offense is attached (if any)". However, when I attempt to join the violations file to the supervision file, using unique youth ID and referral number, most records do not join (fewer than 200 violation records of the 7,000+ in the raw file). All youth in the violations file, however, have at least one supervision record (using the unique youth ID to join the two files). If this is the correct data cleaning approach, does the following logic makes sense for linking a violation to a supervision record: violation_date>=supervision_begin_date & violation_date<=supervision_end_date?

- Do pure duplicates (every value is duplicated across all columns in files) in violations data file indicate multiple violations? Or should we de-duplicate this file?

- Do missing supervision outcomes and supervision end dates indicate youth was under supervision at time of data pull?

- For "Mental health needs status of the listed juvenile" in "Child" file -- does that capture needs status at time of data pull/most recent assessment only? Or does it indicate if youth has ever had documented mental health needs? It appears that the substance use need variable indicates any history that youth have had with substance use services/needs. Is the same true for mental health needs?

- Does supervision period start with disposition? Or can it include pre-disposition detention?

- Do missing values for 'prosecutor_action', 'prosecutor_action_date', 'disposition_date', and 'disposition' in the violations file indicate something specific? Is there a reason these fields are missing for certain violation records? 

- Is there a way to see the original supervision end date at time of initial disposition? (i.e., before any violations or extensions were made to supervision)

- We are currently using phase information from the supervision level file for placement, detention/shelter information -- is this correct?

- What do a supervision phases of "None" and "Warrant" indicate?

- Referral ID, in supervision level and extension files, appears to link back to original referral leading to first supervision disposition -- whereas the referral IDs in the violations, detentions, and placements files seems to link to the most recent referral (in the offense file) that directly pertains to that given violation, detention, or placement. Is this understanding correct? If so, is it okay to join records from these files back to the supervision file via unique youth ID and dates (i.e., if a given placement occurred during a youth's supervision, then it is joined to that supervision?)
